title: Superposition & beats
examples: What causes the sound of beats?
How do I calculate the beat frequency?
Is beat frequency related to wavelength?

explain.say: When two sound waves meet, they overlap in space.
The resulting wave is the sum of the individual waves.
Beats occur when two sound waves of slightly different frequencies meet.
The beat frequency is the absolute difference between the two frequencies.
Phase difference relates to the position in the wave cycle.
In daily life, you hear beats when tuning two similar musical instruments.

faq.q: What is the difference between superposition and beats?
faq.a: Superposition is the general principle that waves combine. Beats are a specific result of superposition when two frequencies are close but not identical.

faq.q: Does the beat frequency depend on the amplitude of the waves?
faq.a: No, the beat frequency depends only on the difference between the two source frequencies. Amplitude affects the loudness, not the beat rate.
asks: Is loudness related to beat frequency?
Does wave strength matter for beats?

faq.q: Can I calculate the phase difference from the beat frequency?
faq.a: You can relate them because frequency is related to phase over time. The relationship involves the angular frequency.
asks: What is the link between phase and beats?
How does time affect the phase difference?

faq.q: If the frequencies are exactly the same, what happens?
faq.a: If the frequencies are identical, the waves will interfere constructively, and you will hear a steady sound with no beats.
asks: Will I hear beats if the sources match?

faq.q: Is the beat frequency measured in Hertz?
faq.a: Yes, beat frequency is a measure of cycles per second, which is the unit Hertz. It is the absolute difference in the source frequencies.
asks: What are the units for beats?
How do I write the unit for beat frequency?

facts: Superposition states that the net displacement at any point is the sum of the individual displacements.
Beats are periodic variations in the loudness of sound caused by interference.
The beat frequency ($f{beat}$) is calculated as the absolute difference: $f{beat} = |f2 - f1|$.
Phase difference describes the relative position of two points on a wave cycle.

quiz.say: Two tuning forks vibrate at 250 Hertz and 254 Hertz. What is the beat frequency?
quiz.why: The beat frequency is the absolute difference between the two given frequencies, which is 4 Hertz.

wrong.0: Dividing the frequencies gives the average frequency, which is not the beat frequency.
wrong.1: Multiplying the frequencies is not a physical calculation for beat frequency.
wrong.3: Adding the frequencies gives the combined maximum frequency, not the beat frequency.

quiz.say: If a wave has a frequency of 100 cycles per second and another has 102 cycles per second, what is the beat frequency?
quiz.why: The beat frequency is the absolute difference between the two frequencies, which is 2 Hertz.

wrong.1: Adding the frequencies gives the maximum possible combined frequency, not the beat frequency.
wrong.2: Halving the difference is incorrect; the beat frequency is the direct difference.
wrong.3: Using the lower frequency ignores the contribution of the higher frequency wave.

quiz.say: When two waves are perfectly in phase, what is the phase difference?
quiz.why: Being perfectly in phase means the waves are at the same point in their cycle, resulting in zero phase difference.

wrong.0: Pi radians represents a phase difference of one half wavelength, not zero.
wrong.1: Two pi radians represents a full cycle, which is equivalent to zero phase difference but is not the simplest answer.
wrong.2: One radian is an arbitrary unit and does not represent the condition of being perfectly in phase.
